system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.
user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    Promo pricing: new accts +31%, booked rev +18%, price-sensitive buyers, first-term renewals -12pp; billing mix constant.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

memory_block.body: Promo pricing: new accts +31%, booked rev +18%, price-sensitive buyers, first-term renewals -12pp; billing mix constant.
Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.
Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.
Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.
Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.
Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

answer.rationale:
The two declines this quarter (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the same self-serve funnel, so the highest-leverage single slot is there rather than at price. Promotional pricing is the tempting answer given the competitor, but memory_73 is the one inherited record that actually measured downstream: +31% new accounts and +18% booked revenue bought at -12pp first-term renewals. Against a 'sustainable long-term qualified revenue' objective that is a known value-destroying trade, and matching an entry-price attack invites a margin race we would not win. Referral incentives (memory_57) target established customers and do not touch the failing funnel; enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is real but addresses a different segment than the one eroding.

I chose simplify_onboarding, but with explicit epistemic caution about the memory it rests on. memory_86 and memory_91 are exactly the shape of claim that degrades under consolidation: both report proxy improvements (completion rate, time-to-value, week-one engagement, 'first meaningful action') and neither records whether those proxies converted into retained, qualified revenue. A shortened onboarding can raise completion simply by removing steps that were doing qualification or expectation-setting work, importing the same first-term-renewal damage memory_73 documents for pricing, just through a metric that looks healthier on the dashboard. So I am spending both verification pulls on memory_86 (the action I intend) and memory_91 (its closest substitute) to recover what the original records measured downstream and over what horizon, and whether 'shortening' meant removing friction or removing qualification. memory_31 corroborates the direction and makes it the better-supported of the two, which is why it is my default if verification is inconclusive.

Scale is a small guarded test, not a broad rollout. The inherited evidence supports a funnel effect; it does not yet support a revenue effect. Guardrails: instrument first-term renewal and 90-day retained revenue as primary, treat completion and activation as secondary, and pre-commit to reverting if activation lifts while downstream retention degrades. If verification shows either memory tracked only week-one proxies, I will treat the expected effect as unproven and keep the test small rather than upgrade it on the strength of a compressed summary.
